result.summary: The pedestrian environment is a narrow urban intersection with mixed-use buildings and faded infrastructure. While sidewalks are present, they are obstructed by utilities and trash bins, and the lack of modern crossing aids like curb ramps or high-visibility markings creates a moderately hostile environment.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk
hazards.description: The painted crosswalk markings are significantly worn, reducing their visibility to approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image, crossing the side street.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: Large trash bins are placed directly on the sidewalk, narrowing the path for pedestrians and those with mobility aids.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-left, on the sidewalk in front of the white building.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: A vehicle parked close to the corner and the building's edge creates a blind spot for pedestrians entering the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Bottom right corner and the building corner on the left.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Repaint the crossing with high-visibility continental markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install standardized curb ramps with tactile warning pads to ensure the crossing is accessible.

result.summary: The image depicts a narrow residential street lined with row houses and sidewalks on both sides. While the narrow geometry may naturally limit vehicle speeds, the environment lacks any marked pedestrian crossings, curb ramps, or traffic control devices, and parked cars significantly obstruct sightlines.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Continuous rows of parked cars on both sides of the street block sightlines between pedestrians attempting to cross and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the visible street length.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no designated or marked areas for pedestrians to cross the street safely, forcing mid-block crossings between parked cars.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near intersections or potential crossing points to improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns to designate pedestrian right-of-way and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions (bulb-outs) at crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position beyond the line of parked cars.

result.summary: This is a narrow, one-way residential street with a marked zebra crosswalk and curb ramps. While the environment is low-speed by design, the lack of stop control at the immediate crossing and presence of parked cars near the intersection create potential visibility issues.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Cars parked close to the crosswalk on the left side of the image may block the sightlines between drivers and pedestrians entering the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street, adjacent to the crosswalk

hazards.name: Lack of Traffic Control
hazards.description: There is no visible stop sign or signal controlling the approach to the crosswalk, relying on driver yielding behavior.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position before they cross.

interventions.title: Raised Crosswalk
interventions.description: Elevate the crosswalk to the level of the sidewalk to act as a speed table and prioritize pedestrian movement.
